lines.quote: Trump’s diesel deal with Putin won’t knock down high prices (page) — unlikely to lower fuel costs (feed)
lines.note: THE HEADLINE: a claim on the object itself — the deal does not deliver; the page hardens the feed’s modal ('unlikely' → 'won’t')
lines.zWhy: the headline asserts the Z-outcome before the record is shown

lines.quote: the deal will probably not lower diesel prices, which soared because of the Iran war and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries
lines.note: THE DEK: two causes named (the war; the refinery strikes) — Carlson’s and MacLean’s two causes in LI register; 'his war' is the one denominating word
lines.zWhy: two structural causes vs one cargo

lines.quote: diesel near record highs; the deal announced last week is unlikely to lower them significantly anytime soon
lines.note: restates the headline with a time clause ('anytime soon') — the first softening
lines.zWhy: 'significantly' and 'anytime soon' leave a door open the headline shut

lines.quote: the volume Russia could supply is far below its own exports a year ago and a small share of what the world lost to the Iran war; delivery itself is uncertain, per energy analysts
lines.note: the mechanism: cargo ÷ hole, plus a delivery doubt — three claims, all sized in the paragraphs that follow
a one-line frame before the numbers — the only paragraph in the lede with no record in it

lines.quote: Russia exported ≈693k bbl/d of diesel Jul–Sep 2025 and ≈140k bbl/d in the same months of 2026 (S&P Global); Trump and Novak promise 300k metric tons for October — roughly 75k bbl/d
lines.note: SIZES THE CARGO against Russia’s own prior — the deal restores about an eighth of what Russia itself used to ship; the one conversion (tons → bbl/d) is the lede’s key move
lines.zWhy: 75k against 693k reads the deal as small on its own terms

lines.quote: the Middle East exported 809k fewer bbl/d of diesel Jul–Sep than in 2025, since the US and Israel began attacking Iran on Feb 28 (S&P Global); the deal looks 'even more meager' against that
lines.note: SIZES THE HOLE: the cargo is under a tenth of the Gulf’s lost barrels; 'meager' the one adjective; the war dated to the day

lines.quote: “The main issue is still the Strait of Hormuz” — Sarah Raffoul, Argus
lines.note: THE CHALLENGE: the deal read against the Strait rather than against Russia — the analyst moves the object; cross-reads to H6 (the Hormuz control claim)
lines.zWhy: if the issue is the Strait, a Russian cargo is the wrong instrument

lines.quote: the Middle East + Russia shortfall is the main reason diesel is up ≈77% this year
lines.note: closes the record: the price sized, the cause named — then the paywall
lines.zWhy: the cause of a 77% rise is not a 75k bbl/d cargo
